basis: Umbrella disorder of a reproductive organ; endocrine dysfunction is not a defining feature across the group.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with impaired sperm production and motility; reproductive function has no axis.
Peripheral neuropathy and optic atrophy define disease; fixed pes cavus and hammertoes occur in 5/5, with claw-hand deformity in 3/5.
Benign tumour of vulvar vestibular glands, including Bartholin glands; reproductive location, unrelated to the vestibular ear.
Blepharophimosis and intellectual disability define syndrome; seizures are frequent. Adducted thumbs alone do not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Inherited red-cell membrane disease causing hemolysis; gallstones are a separate disease, while jaundice and hepatomegaly alone do not establish liver damage.
Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy defines skeletal thoracic restriction and respiratory dysfunction; renal damage is not established for this subtype.
Intrahepatic biliary atresia directly affects bile ducts; unspecified syndromic status does not establish additional organs.
Corneal dystrophy, ichthyosis and microcephaly with intellectual disability define eye, skin and brain involvement.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; minor dysmorphic features do not establish additional organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental, cardiac and skeletal defects define syndrome; reflux/hydronephrosis occur in 30-79%; common oral/dental abnormalities omitted by cap.
Lysosomal lipid storage causes progressive CNS disease in most and common hepatic storage disease (~50%); splenic/marrow deposits alone lack proven functional damage.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly/ID and skin/hair atrophy define syndrome; pyloric atresia reported in 80-99%; ptosis 80-99% omitted by cap.
Developmental brain disorder; atrial septal defects and anemia/thrombocytopenia each occur in 30-79%; recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
BRAF-mutant anaplastic pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma is a primary CNS astrocytic tumour.
Primary microcephaly with intellectual disability; strabismus and structural external-ear hypoplasia (microtia) each reported in 2/2 patients.
Photomyoclonus/cerebral dysfunction, diabetes and nephropathy define syndrome; deafness is also a defining feature and meets the diagnostic-criterion exception.
Malignancy arising in eyelid skin; eyelids belong to the ocular axis and the tumour's cutaneous origin supports dermatologic.
Radial hypoplasia, nasal airway obstruction from choanal atresia and convergent strabismus are defining features.
Hamartomatous polyp principally occupying gastrointestinal mucosa; nasopharyngeal and urinary locations are rare.
Defining myopathy, intellectual disability and urethral malformation (hypospadias); growth delay alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Acquired coagulation factor deficiency; an immune mechanism is not universal, and underlying liver disease is a separate condition.
Cleft palate, intellectual disability and limb abnormalities are defining features in the supplied syndrome description.
IgM-producing lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving marrow; symptomatic neuropathy and hyperviscosity organ injury generally affect fewer than 30%.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis; no other organ involvement is universal across subtypes.
